## About Me

::: {.highlight-box}
My research develops computational models for resilient infrastructure systems and the built environment, integrating AI, optimization, risk and loss modeling, and decision analysis to support risk-informed decisions.
:::

<p style="font-size:1.05rem; margin-top:0.9rem; margin-bottom:1.5rem; font-weight:500;">
  ✨ I am on the <strong>2026–2027 academic job market</strong> for faculty positions!
</p>

I am a Postdoctoral Researcher at the [CHEER Hub](https://www.drc.udel.edu/cheer/) within the Disaster Research Center at the University of Delaware. I work with [Rachel Davidson](https://ccee.udel.edu/faculty/rachel-davidson/) and [Linda Nozick](https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/people/linda-k-nozick/) on computational models that integrate hazard and loss modeling, evolving exposure, infrastructure systems, stakeholder decision-making, and policy design. 

I earned my Ph.D. in Industrial Engineering from Purdue University, advised by [David Johnson](https://engineering.purdue.edu/IE/people/ptProfile?resource_id=126281). My doctoral work developed data-driven and optimization-based adaptive infrastructure strategies under deep uncertainty and contributed to risk assessment models used in Louisiana’s Coastal Master Plan.

Across my work, I am interested in how engineering models can better inform decisions under uncertainty: which risks we measure, which interventions we prioritize, and how the benefits and costs of those decisions are distributed across communities, households, insurers, and public agencies.

My work has been recognized through research awards, competitive funding, and professional leadership. I have served as Chair of the [Engineering and Infrastructure Specialty Group](https://www.sra.org/risk-analysis-specialty-groups/engineering-and-infrastructure/) of the Society for Risk Analysis and was named an [NSF Ocean Decade Champion](https://www.nsf.gov/news/supporting-women-ocean-sciences).

## News

- **Aug 2026:** Our paper, [*An Optimization-Based Approach to Developing Computationally Efficient Long-Term Event-Loss Scenario Ensembles*](https://ascelibrary.org/doi/10.1061/AJRUA6.RUENG-2004), is now available in the *ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems, Part A: Civil Engineering*.

- **Aug 2026:** Our paper, [*Coupling Land Use Planning and Multi-Stakeholder Dynamics to Inform Disaster Risk Management: Who Pays for Risk and Who Gains from Intervention?*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106222), is now available in the *International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction*.

- **May 2026:** Research spotlight presentation at the NHERI Computational Symposium on computational methods for modeling long-term sequences of hazard losses and their implications for recovery and resilience.

- **May 2026:** Our paper, [*Stakeholder Dynamics in Disaster Mitigation Funding: The Roles of Timing, Spatial Scale and Allocation Basis in Policy Design*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106120), was published in the *International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction*.

- **Dec 2025:** Presented first-authored research at the Society for Risk Analysis Annual Meeting on how land-use planning and multi-stakeholder dynamics shape disaster risk and its distribution.
